texts.2co.9.6: But this I say, He who soweth sparingly, shall reap also sparingly; and he who soweth bountifully, shall reap also bountifully.
texts.2co.9.7: Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or by constraint: for God loveth a cheerful giver.
texts.2co.9.8: And God is able to make all grace abound towards you; that ye always having all sufficiency in all things, may abound to every good work:
texts.2co.9.9: (As it is written, He hath dispersed; he hath given to the poor: his righteousness remaineth for ever.
texts.2co.9.10: Now may he that ministereth seed to the sower, both minister bread for your food, and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness;)
texts.2co.9.11: Being enriched in every thing to all bountifulness, which causeth through us thanksgiving to God.
texts.2co.9.12: For the administration of this service not only supplieth the want of the saints, but is abundant also by many thanksgivings to God;
texts.2co.9.13: While by the experiment of this ministration they glorify God for your professed subjection to the gospel of Christ, and for your liberal distribution to them, and to all men;
texts.2co.9.14: And by their prayer for you, who long after you, for the exceeding grace of God in you.
texts.2co.9.15: Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift.
texts.2co.10.1: Now I Paul myself beseech you, by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, who in presence am base among you, but being absent am bold towards you:
texts.2co.10.2: But I beseech you, that I may not be bold when I am present with that confidence, with which I think to be bold against some, who think of us as if we walked according to the flesh.
texts.2co.10.3: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh:
texts.2co.10.4: (For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds;)
texts.2co.10.5: Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ;
texts.2co.10.6: And having in a readiness to avenge all disobedience, when your obedience is fulfilled.
texts.2co.10.7: Do ye look on things after the outward appearance? If any man trusteth to himself that he is Christ's, let him of himself think this again, that, as he is Christ's, even so are we Christ's.
texts.2co.10.8: For though I should boast somewhat more of our authority, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I should not be ashamed:
texts.2co.10.9: That I may not seem as if I would terrify you by letters.
texts.2co.10.10: For his letters (say they) are weighty and powerful; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech contemptible.
texts.2co.10.11: Let such one think this, that such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such will we be also in deed when we are present.
texts.2co.10.12: For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise.
texts.2co.10.13: But we will not boast of things without our measure, but according to the measure of the rule which God hath distributed to us, a measure to reach even to you.
texts.2co.10.14: For we stretch not ourselves beyond our measure, as though we reached not to you; for we are come as far as to you also in preaching the gospel of Christ:
texts.2co.10.15: Not boasting of things without our measure, that is, of other men's labors; but having hope, when your faith is increased, that we shall be enlarged by you, according to our rule abundantly,
texts.2co.10.16: To preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another man's line of things made ready to our hand.
texts.2co.10.17: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.
texts.2co.10.18: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.
texts.2co.11.1: I earnestly wish ye could bear with me a little in my folly: and indeed bear with me.
texts.2co.11.2: For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.
texts.2co.11.3: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty, so your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity that is in Christ.
texts.2co.11.4: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or if ye receive another spirit, which ye have not received, or another gospel, which ye have not accepted, ye might well bear with him.
texts.2co.11.5: For I suppose I was not a whit behind the very greatest apostles.
texts.2co.11.6: But though I am rude in speech, yet not in knowledge; but we have been thoroughly made manifest among you in all things.
texts.2co.11.7: Have I committed an offense in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I have preached to you the gospel of God without reward?
texts.2co.11.8: I robbed other churches, taking wages of them, to do you service.
texts.2co.11.9: And when I was present with you, and wanted, I was chargeable to no man: for that which was lacking to me the brethren who came from Macedonia supplied: and in all things I have kept myself from being burdensome to you, and so will I keep myself.
texts.2co.11.10: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this boasting in the regions of Achaia.
texts.2co.11.11: Why? because I love you not? God knoweth.
texts.2co.11.12: But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them who desire occasion; that in what they glory, they may be found even as we.
texts.2co.11.13: For such are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into the apostles of Christ.
texts.2co.11.14: And no wonder; for Satan himself is transformed into an angel of light.
texts.2co.11.15: Therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also are transformed as the ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.
texts.2co.11.16: I say again, Let no man think me a fool; if otherwise, yet as a fool receive me, that I may boast myself a little.
texts.2co.11.17: That which I speak, I speak it not according to the Lord, but as it were foolishly, in this confidence of boasting.
texts.2co.11.18: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.
texts.2co.11.19: For ye suffer fools gladly, seeing ye yourselves are wise.
texts.2co.11.20: For ye suffer, if a man bringeth you into bondage, if a man devoureth you, if a man taketh from you, if a man exalteth himself, if a man smiteth you on the face.
texts.2co.11.21: I speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak. But in whatever respect any is bold, (I speak foolishly) I am bold also.
texts.2co.11.22: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the offspring of Abraham? so am I.
texts.2co.11.23: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as a fool) I am more; in labors more abundant, in stripes above measure, in prisons more frequent, in deaths often.
texts.2co.11.24: From the Jews five times I received forty stripes save one.
texts.2co.11.25: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once I was stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have been in the deep;
texts.2co.11.26: In journeyings often, in perils of waters, in perils of robbers, in perils by my own countrymen, in perils by the heathen, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;
texts.2co.11.27: In weariness and painfulness, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
texts.2co.11.28: Besides those things that are without, that which cometh upon me daily, the care of all the churches.
texts.2co.11.29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is made to fall into sin, and I burn not?
texts.2co.11.30: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things which concern my infirmities.
texts.2co.11.31: The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who is blessed for evermore, knoweth that I lie not.
texts.2co.11.32: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes with a garrison, desirous to apprehend me:
texts.2co.11.33: And through a window in a basket I was let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.
texts.2co.12.1: It is not expedient for me doubtless to glory. I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
texts.2co.12.2: I knew a man in Christ above fourteen years ago, (whether in the body, I cannot tell; or whether out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;) such one caught up to the third heaven.
texts.2co.12.3: And I knew such a man, (whether in the body, or out of the body, I cannot tell: God knoweth;)
texts.2co.12.4: That he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.
texts.2co.12.5: Of such one will I glory: yet of myself I will not glory, but in my infirmities.
texts.2co.12.6: For though I would desire to glory, I shall not be a fool; for I will say the truth: but now I forbear, lest any man should think of me above that which he seeth me to be, or what he heareth from me.
texts.2co.12.7: And lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me, lest I should be exalted above measure.
texts.2co.12.8: For this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.
texts.2co.12.9: And he said to me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
texts.2co.12.10: Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
texts.2co.12.11: I am become a fool in glorying; ye have compelled me: for I ought to have been commended by you: for in nothing am I behind the very greatest apostles, though I am nothing.
texts.2co.12.12: Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, in signs, and wonders, and mighty deeds.
texts.2co.12.13: For what is that in which ye were inferior to other churches, except that I myself was not burdensome to you? forgive me this wrong.
texts.2co.12.14: Behold, the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be burdensome to you: for I seek not yours, but you. For the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
texts.2co.12.15: And I will very gladly spend and be spent for you; though the more abundantly I love you, the less I am loved.
texts.2co.12.16: But be it so, I did not burden you: nevertheless, being crafty, I caught you with guile.
texts.2co.12.17: Did I make a gain of you by any of them whom I sent to you?
texts.2co.12.18: I desired Titus, and with him I sent a brother. Did Titus make a gain of you? walked we not in the same spirit? walked we not in the same steps?
texts.2co.12.19: Again, think ye that we excuse ourselves to you? we speak before God in Christ: but we do all things, dearly beloved, for your edification.
texts.2co.12.20: For I fear, lest, when I come, I shall not find you such as I would, and that I shall be found by you such as ye would not: lest there be debates, envyings, wraths, strifes, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults:
texts.2co.12.21: And lest, when I come again, my God may humble me among you, and I shall bewail many who have sinned already, and have not repented of the uncleanness, and lewdness, and lasciviousness, which they have committed.
texts.2co.13.1: This is the third time I am coming to you: By the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every word be established.
texts.2co.13.2: I told you before, and foretell you, as if I were present, the second time; and being absent now I write to them who heretofore have sinned, and to all others, that, if I come again, I will not spare;
texts.2co.13.3: Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, who toward you is not weak, but is mighty in you.
texts.2co.13.4: For though he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth by the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him by the power of God towards you.
texts.2co.13.5: Examine yourselves, whether ye are in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye are reprobates?
texts.2co.13.6: But I trust that ye will know that we are not reprobates.
texts.2co.13.7: Now I pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we should appear approved, but that ye should do that which is honest, though we should be as reprobates.
texts.2co.13.8: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
texts.2co.13.9: For we are glad, when we are weak, and ye are strong: and this also we wish, even your perfection.
texts.2co.13.10: Therefore I write these things being absent, lest being present I should use sharpness, according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.
texts.2co.13.11: Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfect, be of good comfort, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace will be with you.
texts.2co.13.12: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
texts.2co.13.14: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, be with you all. Amen.

texts.2co.1.1: Paul, apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, and the brother Timotheus, to the assembly of God which is in Corinth, with all the saints who are in the whole of Achaia.
texts.2co.1.2: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and [the] Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.2co.1.3: Blessed [be] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassions, and God of all encouragement;
texts.2co.1.4: who encourages us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to encourage those who are in any tribulation whatever, through the encouragement with which we ourselves are encouraged of God.
texts.2co.1.5: Because, even as the sufferings of the Christ abound towards us, so through the Christ does our encouragement also abound.
texts.2co.1.6: But whether we are in tribulation, [it is] for your encouragement and salvation, wrought in the endurance of the same sufferings which *we* also suffer,
texts.2co.1.7: (and our hope for you [is] sure;) or whether we are encouraged, [it is] for your encouragement and salvation: knowing that as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so also of the encouragement.
texts.2co.1.8: For we do not wish you to be ignorant, brethren, as to our tribulation which happened [to us] in Asia, that we were excessively pressed beyond [our] power, so as to despair even of living.
texts.2co.1.9: But we ourselves had the sentence of death in ourselves, that we should not have our trust in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead;
texts.2co.1.10: who has delivered us from so great a death, and does deliver; in whom we confide that he will also yet deliver;
texts.2co.1.11: ye also labouring together by supplication for us that the gift towards us, through means of many persons, may be the subject of the thanksgiving of many for us.
texts.2co.1.12: For our boasting is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and sincerity before God, (not in fleshly wisdom but in God's grace,) we have had our conversation in the world, and more abundantly towards you.
texts.2co.1.13: For we do not write other things to you but what ye well know and recognise; and I hope that ye will recognise to the end,
texts.2co.1.14: even as also ye have recognised us in part, that we are your boast, even as *ye* [are] ours in the day of the Lord Jesus.
texts.2co.1.15: And with this confidence I purposed to come to you previously, that ye might have a second favour;
texts.2co.1.16: and to pass through to Macedonia by you, and again from Macedonia to come to you, and to be set forward by you to Judaea.
texts.2co.1.17: Having therefore this purpose, did I then use lightness? Or what I purpose, do I purpose according to flesh, that there should be with me yea yea, and nay nay?
texts.2co.1.18: Now God [is] faithful, that our word to you is not yea and nay.
texts.2co.1.19: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, he who has been preached by us among you (by me and Silvanus and Timotheus), did not become yea and nay, but yea *is* in him.
texts.2co.1.20: For whatever promises of God [there are], in him is the yea, and in him the amen, for glory to God by us.
texts.2co.1.21: Now he that establishes us with you in Christ, and has anointed us, [is] God,
texts.2co.1.22: who also has sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.
texts.2co.1.23: But I call God to witness upon my soul that to spare you I have not yet come to Corinth.
texts.2co.1.24: Not that we rule over your faith, but are fellow-workmen of your joy: for by faith ye stand.
texts.2co.2.1: But I have judged this with myself, not to come back to you in grief.
texts.2co.2.2: For if *I* grieve you, who also [is] it that gladdens me, if not he that is grieved through me?
texts.2co.2.3: And I have written this very [letter] [to you], that coming I may not have grief from those from whom I ought to have joy; trusting in you all that my joy is [that] of you all.
texts.2co.2.4: For out of much tribulation and distress of heart I wrote to you, with many tears; not that ye may be grieved, but that ye may know the love which I have very abundantly towards you.
texts.2co.2.5: But if any one has grieved, he has grieved, not me, but in part (that I may not overcharge [you]) all of you.
texts.2co.2.6: Sufficient to such a one [is] this rebuke which [has been inflicted] by the many;
texts.2co.2.7: so that on the contrary ye should rather shew grace and encourage, lest perhaps such a one should be swallowed up with excessive grief.
texts.2co.2.8: Wherefore I exhort you to assure him of [your] love.
texts.2co.2.9: For to this end also I have written, that I might know, by putting you to the test, if as to everything ye are obedient.
texts.2co.2.10: But to whom ye forgive anything, *I* also; for I also, what I have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, [it is] for your sakes in [the] person of Christ;
texts.2co.2.11: that we might not have Satan get an advantage against us, for we are not ignorant of *his* thoughts.
texts.2co.2.12: Now when I came to Troas for the [publication of the] glad tidings of the Christ, a door also being opened to me in [the] Lord,
texts.2co.2.13: I had no rest in my spirit at not finding Titus my brother; but bidding them adieu, I came away to Macedonia.
texts.2co.2.14: But thanks [be] to God, who always leads us in triumph in the Christ, and makes manifest the odour of his knowledge through us in every place.
texts.2co.2.15: For we are a sweet odour of Christ to God, in the saved and in those that perish:
texts.2co.2.16: to the one an odour from death unto death, but to the others an odour from life unto life; and who [is] sufficient for these things?
texts.2co.2.17: For we do not, as the many, make a trade of the word of God; but as of sincerity, but as of God, before God, we speak in Christ.
texts.2co.3.1: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or do we need, as some, commendatory letters to you, or [commendatory] from you?
texts.2co.3.2: *Ye* are our letter, written in our hearts, known and read of all men,
texts.2co.3.3: being manifested to be Christ's epistle ministered by us, written, not with ink, but [the] Spirit of [the] living God; not on stone tables, but on fleshy tables of [the] heart.
texts.2co.3.4: And such confidence have we through the Christ towards God:
texts.2co.3.5: not that we are competent of ourselves to think anything as of ourselves, but our competency [is] of God;
texts.2co.3.6: who has also made us competent, [as] ministers of [the] new covenant; not of letter, but of spirit. For the letter kills, but the Spirit quickens.
texts.2co.3.7: (But if the ministry of death, in letters, graven in stones, began with glory, so that the children of Israel could not fix their eyes on the face of Moses, on account of the glory of his face, [a glory] which is annulled;
texts.2co.3.8: how shall not rather the ministry of the Spirit subsist in glory?
texts.2co.3.9: For if the ministry of condemnation [be] glory, much rather the ministry of righteousness abounds in glory.
texts.2co.3.10: For also that [which was] glorified is not glorified in this respect, on account of the surpassing glory.
texts.2co.3.11: For if that annulled [was introduced] with glory, much rather that which abides [subsists] in glory.
texts.2co.3.12: Having therefore such hope, we use much boldness:
texts.2co.3.13: and not according as Moses put a veil on his own face, so that the children of Israel should not fix their eyes on the end of that annulled.
texts.2co.3.14: But their thoughts have been darkened, for unto this day the same veil remains in reading the old covenant, unremoved, which in Christ is annulled.
texts.2co.3.15: But unto this day, when Moses is read, the veil lies upon their heart.
texts.2co.3.16: But when it shall turn to [the] Lord, the veil is taken away.)
texts.2co.3.17: Now the Lord is the Spirit, but where the Spirit of [the] Lord [is, there is] liberty.
texts.2co.3.18: But *we* all, looking on the glory of the Lord, with unveiled face, are transformed according to the same image from glory to glory, even as by [the] Lord [the] Spirit.
texts.2co.4.1: Therefore, having this ministry, as we have had mercy shewn us, we faint not.
texts.2co.4.2: But we have rejected the hidden things of shame, not walking in deceit, nor falsifying the word of God, but by manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every conscience of men before God.
texts.2co.4.3: But if also our gospel is veiled, it is veiled in those that are lost;
texts.2co.4.4: in whom the god of this world has blinded the thoughts of the unbelieving, so that the radiancy of the glad tidings of the glory of the Christ, who is [the] image of God, should not shine forth [for them].
texts.2co.4.5: For we do not preach ourselves, but Christ Jesus Lord, and ourselves your bondmen for Jesus' sake.
texts.2co.4.6: Because [it is] the God who spoke that out of darkness light should shine who has shone in our hearts for the shining forth of the knowledge of the glory of God in [the] face of [Jesus] Christ.
texts.2co.4.7: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the surpassingness of the power may be of God, and not from us:
texts.2co.4.8: every way afflicted, but not straitened; seeing no apparent issue, but our way not entirely shut up;
texts.2co.4.9: persecuted, but not abandoned; cast down, but not destroyed;
texts.2co.4.10: always bearing about in the body the dying of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our body;
texts.2co.4.11: for we who live are always delivered unto death on account of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our mortal flesh;
texts.2co.4.12: so that death works in us, but life in you.
texts.2co.4.13: And having the same spirit of faith, according to what is written, I have believed, therefore have I spoken; *we* also believe, therefore also we speak;
texts.2co.4.14: knowing that he who has raised the Lord Jesus shall raise us also with Jesus, and shall present [us] with you.
texts.2co.4.15: For all things [are] for your sakes, that the grace abounding through the many may cause thanksgiving to abound to the glory of God.
texts.2co.4.16: Wherefore we faint not; but if indeed our outward man is consumed, yet the inward is renewed day by day.
texts.2co.4.17: For our momentary [and] light affliction works for us in surpassing measure an eternal weight of glory;
texts.2co.4.18: while we look not at the things that are seen, but at the things that are not seen; for the things that are seen [are] for a time, but those that are not seen eternal.
texts.2co.5.1: For we know that if our earthly tabernacle house be destroyed, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
texts.2co.5.2: For indeed in this we groan, ardently desiring to have put on our house which [is] from heaven;
texts.2co.5.3: if indeed being also clothed we shall not be found naked.
texts.2co.5.4: For indeed we who are in the tabernacle groan, being burdened; while yet we do not wish to be unclothed, but clothed, that [what is] mortal may be swallowed up by life.
texts.2co.5.5: Now he that has wrought us for this very thing [is] God, who also has given to us the earnest of the Spirit.
texts.2co.5.6: Therefore [we are] always confident, and know that while present in the body we are absent from the Lord,
texts.2co.5.7: (for we walk by faith, not by sight;)
texts.2co.5.8: we are confident, I say, and pleased rather to be absent from the body and present with the Lord.
texts.2co.5.9: Wherefore also we are zealous, whether present or absent, to be agreeable to him.
texts.2co.5.10: For we must all be manifested before the judgment-seat of the Christ, that each may receive the things [done] in the body, according to those he has done, whether [it be] good or evil.
texts.2co.5.11: Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord we persuade men, but have been manifested to God, and I hope also that we have been manifested in your consciences.
texts.2co.5.12: [For] we do not again commend ourselves to you, but [we are] giving to you occasion of boast in our behalf, that ye may have [such] with those boasting in countenance, and not in heart.
texts.2co.5.13: For whether we are beside ourselves, [it is] to God; or are sober, [it is] for you.
texts.2co.5.14: For the love of the Christ constrains us, having judged this: that one died for all, then all have died;
texts.2co.5.15: and he died for all, that they who live should no longer live to themselves, but to him who died for them and has been raised.
texts.2co.5.16: So that *we* henceforth know no one according to flesh; but if even we have known Christ according to flesh, yet now we know [him thus] no longer.
texts.2co.5.17: So if any one [be] in Christ, [there is] a new creation; the old things have passed away; behold all things have become new:
texts.2co.5.18: and all things [are] of the God who has reconciled us to himself by [Jesus] Christ, and given to us the ministry of that reconciliation:
texts.2co.5.19: how that God was in Christ, reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their offences; and putting in us the word of that reconciliation.
texts.2co.5.20: We are ambassadors therefore for Christ, God as [it were] beseeching by us, we entreat for Christ, Be reconciled to God.
texts.2co.5.21: Him who knew not sin he has made sin for us, that *we* might become God's righteousness in him.
texts.2co.6.1: But [as] fellow-workmen, we also beseech that ye receive not the grace of God in vain:
texts.2co.6.2: (for he says, I have listened to thee in an accepted time, and I have helped thee in a day of salvation: behold, now [is the] well-accepted time; behold, now [the] day of salvation:)
texts.2co.6.3: giving no manner of offence in anything, that the ministry be not blamed;
texts.2co.6.4: but in everything commending ourselves as God's ministers, in much endurance, in afflictions, in necessities, in straits,
texts.2co.6.5: in stripes, in prisons, in riots, in labours, in watchings, in fastings,
texts.2co.6.6: in pureness, in knowledge, in longsuffering, in kindness, in [the] Holy Spirit, in love unfeigned,
texts.2co.6.7: in [the] word of truth, in [the] power of God; through the arms of righteousness on the right hand and left,
texts.2co.6.8: through glory and dishonour, through evil report and good report: as deceivers, and true;
texts.2co.6.9: as unknown, and well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as disciplined, and not put to death;
texts.2co.6.10: as grieved, but always rejoicing; as poor, but enriching many; as having nothing, and possessing all things.
texts.2co.6.11: Our mouth is opened to you, Corinthians, our heart is expanded.
texts.2co.6.12: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your affections;
texts.2co.6.13: but for an answering recompense, (I speak as to children,) let *your* heart also expand itself.
texts.2co.6.14: Be not diversely yoked with unbelievers; for what participation [is there] between righteousness and lawlessness? or what fellowship of light with darkness?
texts.2co.6.15: and what consent of Christ with Beliar, or what part for a believer along with an unbeliever?
texts.2co.6.16: and what agreement of God's temple with idols? for *ye* are [the] living God's temple; according as God has said, I will dwell among them, and walk among [them]; and I will be their God, and they shall be to me a people.
texts.2co.6.17: Wherefore come out from the midst of them, and be separated, saith [the] Lord, and touch not [what is] unclean, and *I* will receive you;
texts.2co.6.18: and I will be to you for a Father, and ye shall be to me for sons and daughters, saith [the] Lord Almighty.
texts.2co.7.1: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let us purify ourselves from every pollution of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in God's fear.
texts.2co.7.2: Receive us: we have injured no one, we have ruined no one, we have made gain of no one.
texts.2co.7.3: I do not speak for condemnation, for I have already said that ye are in our hearts, to die together, and live together.
texts.2co.7.4: Great [is] my boldness towards you, great my exulting in respect of you; I am filled with encouragement; I overabound in joy under all our affliction.
texts.2co.7.5: For indeed, when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no rest, but [we were] afflicted in every way; without combats, within fears.
texts.2co.7.6: But he who encourages those that are [brought] low, [even] God, encouraged us by the coming of Titus;
texts.2co.7.7: and not by his coming only, but also through the encouragement with which he was encouraged as to you; relating to us your ardent desire, your mourning, your zeal for me; so that I the more rejoiced.
texts.2co.7.8: For if also I grieved you in the letter, I do not regret [it], if even I have regretted it; for I see that that letter, if even [it were] only for a time, grieved you.
texts.2co.7.9: Now I rejoice, not that ye have been grieved, but that ye have been grieved to repentance; for ye have been grieved according to God, that in nothing ye might be injured by us.
texts.2co.7.10: For grief according to God works repentance to salvation, never to be regretted; but the grief of the world works death.
texts.2co.7.11: For, behold, this same thing, your being grieved according to God, how much diligence it wrought in *you*, but [what] excusing [of yourselves], but [what] indignation, but [what] fear, but [what] ardent desire, but [what] zeal, but [what] vengeance: in every way ye have proved yourselves to be pure in the matter.
texts.2co.7.12: So then, if also I wrote to you, [it was] not for the sake of him that injured, nor for the sake of him that was injured, but for the sake of our diligent zeal for you being manifested to you before God.
texts.2co.7.13: For this reason we have been encouraged. And we the rather rejoiced in our encouragement more abundantly by reason of the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by you all.
texts.2co.7.14: Because if I boasted to him anything about you, I have not been put to shame; but as we have spoken to you all things in truth, so also our boasting to Titus has been [the] truth;
texts.2co.7.15: and his affections are more abundantly towards you, calling to mind the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye received him.
texts.2co.7.16: I rejoice that in everything I am confident as to you.
texts.2co.8.1: But we make known to you, brethren, the grace of God bestowed in the assemblies of Macedonia;
texts.2co.8.2: that in a great trial of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty has abounded to the riches of their [free-hearted] liberality.
texts.2co.8.3: For according to [their] power, I bear witness, and beyond [their] power, [they were] willing of their own accord,
texts.2co.8.4: begging of us with much entreaty [to give effect to] the grace and fellowship of the service which [was to be rendered] to the saints.
texts.2co.8.5: And not according as we hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord, and to us by God's will.
texts.2co.8.6: So that we begged Titus that, according as he had before begun, so he would also complete as to you this grace also;
texts.2co.8.7: but even as ye abound in every way, in faith, and word, and knowledge, and all diligence, and in love from you to us, that ye may abound in this grace also.
texts.2co.8.8: I do not speak as commanding [it], but through the zeal of others, and proving the genuineness of your love.
texts.2co.8.9: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that for your sakes he, being rich, became poor, in order that *ye* by *his* poverty might be enriched.
texts.2co.8.10: And I give [my] opinion in this, for this is profitable for you who began before, not only to do, but also to be willing, a year ago.
texts.2co.8.11: But now also complete the doing of it; so that as [there was] the readiness to be willing, so also to complete out of what ye have.
texts.2co.8.12: For if the readiness be there, [a man is] accepted according to what he may have, not according to what he has not.
texts.2co.8.13: For [it is] not in order that there may be ease for others, and for you distress,
texts.2co.8.14: but [on the principle] of equality; in the present time your abundance for their lack, that their abundance may be for your lack, so that there should be equality.
texts.2co.8.15: According as it is written, He who [gathered] much had no excess, and he who [gathered] little was nothing short.
texts.2co.8.16: But thanks [be] to God, who gives the same diligent zeal for you in the heart of Titus.
texts.2co.8.17: For he received indeed the entreaty, but, being full of zeal, he went of his own accord to you;
texts.2co.8.18: but we have sent with him the brother whose praise [is] in the glad tidings through all the assemblies;
texts.2co.8.19: and not only [so], but [is] also chosen by the assemblies as our fellow-traveller with this grace, ministered by us to the glory of the Lord himself, and [a witness of] our readiness;
texts.2co.8.20: avoiding this, that any one should blame us in this abundance [which is] administered by us;
texts.2co.8.21: for we provide for things honest, not only before [the] Lord, but also before men.
texts.2co.8.22: And we have sent with them our brother whom we have often proved to be of diligent zeal in many things, and now more diligently zealous through the great confidence [he has] as to you.
texts.2co.8.23: Whether as regards Titus, [he is] my companion and fellow-labourer in your behalf; or our brethren, [they are] deputed messengers of assemblies, Christ's glory.
texts.2co.8.24: Shew therefore to them, before the assemblies, the proof of your love, and of our boasting about you.
texts.2co.9.1: For concerning the ministration which [is] for the saints, it is superfluous my writing to you.
texts.2co.9.2: For I know your readiness, which I boast of as respects you to Macedonians, that Achaia is prepared since a year ago, and the zeal [reported] of you has stimulated the mass [of the brethren].
texts.2co.9.3: But I have sent the brethren, in order that our boasting about you may not be made void in this respect, in order that, as I have said, ye may be prepared;
texts.2co.9.4: lest haply, if Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, *we*, that we say not *ye*, may be put to shame in this confidence.
texts.2co.9.5: I thought it necessary therefore to beg the brethren that they would come to you, and complete beforehand your fore-announced blessing, that this may be ready thus as blessing, and not as got out of you.
texts.2co.9.6: But this [is true], he that sows sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he that sows in [the spirit of] blessing shall reap also in blessing:
texts.2co.9.7: each according as he is purposed in his heart; not grievingly, or of necessity; for God loves a cheerful giver.
texts.2co.9.8: But God is able to make every gracious gift abound towards you, that, having in every way always all-sufficiency, ye may abound to every good work:
texts.2co.9.9: according as it is written, He has scattered abroad, he has given to the poor, his righteousness remains for ever.
texts.2co.9.10: Now he that supplies seed to the sower and bread for eating shall supply and make abundant your sowing, and increase the fruits of your righteousness:
texts.2co.9.11: enriched in every way unto all free-hearted liberality, which works through us thanksgiving to God.
texts.2co.9.12: Because the ministration of this service is not only filling up the measure of what is lacking to the saints, but also abounding by many thanksgivings to God;
texts.2co.9.13: they glorifying God through the proof of this ministration, by reason of your subjection, by profession, to the glad tidings of the Christ, and your free-hearted liberality in communicating towards them and towards all;
texts.2co.9.14: and in their supplication for you, full of ardent desire for you, on account of the exceeding grace of God [which is] upon you.
texts.2co.9.15: Thanks [be] to God for his unspeakable free gift.
texts.2co.10.1: But I myself, Paul, entreat you by the meekness and gentleness of the Christ, who, as to appearance, [when present] [am] mean among you, but absent am bold towards you;
texts.2co.10.2: but I beseech that present I may not be bold with the confidence with which I think to be daring towards some who think of us as walking according to flesh.
texts.2co.10.3: For walking in flesh, we do not war according to flesh.
texts.2co.10.4: For the arms of our warfare [are] not fleshly, but powerful according to God to [the] overthrow of strongholds;
texts.2co.10.5: overthrowing reasonings and every high thing that lifts itself up against the knowledge of God, and leading captive every thought into the obedience of the Christ;
texts.2co.10.6: and having in readiness to avenge all disobedience when your obedience shall have been fulfilled.
texts.2co.10.7: Do ye look at what concerns appearance? If any one has confidence in himself that he is of Christ, let him think this again in himself, that even as he [is] of Christ, so also [are] we.
texts.2co.10.8: For and if I should boast even somewhat more abundantly of our authority, which the Lord has given [to us] for building up and not for your overthrowing, I shall not be put to shame;
texts.2co.10.9: that I may not seem as if I was frightening you by letters:
texts.2co.10.10: because his letters, he says, [are] weighty and strong, but his presence in the body weak, and his speech naught.
texts.2co.10.11: Let such a one think this, that such as we are in word by letters [when] absent, such also present in deed.
texts.2co.10.12: For we dare not class ourselves or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves; but these, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are not intelligent.
texts.2co.10.13: Now *we* will not boast out of measure, but according to the measure of the rule which the God of measure has apportioned to us, to reach to you also.
texts.2co.10.14: For we do not, as not reaching to you, overstretch ourselves, (for we have come to you also in the glad tidings of the Christ;)
texts.2co.10.15: not boasting out of measure in other people's labours, but having hope, your faith increasing, to be enlarged amongst you, according to our rule, yet more abundantly
texts.2co.10.16: to announce the glad tidings to that [which is] beyond you, not to be boasting in another's rule of things made ready to hand.
texts.2co.10.17: But he that boasts, let him boast in the Lord.
texts.2co.10.18: For not *he* that commends himself is approved, but whom the Lord commends.
texts.2co.11.1: Would that ye would bear with me [in] a little folly; but indeed bear with me.
texts.2co.11.2: For I am jealous as to you with a jealousy [which is] of God; for I have espoused you unto one man, to present [you] a chaste virgin to Christ.
texts.2co.11.3: But I fear lest by any means, as the serpent deceived Eve by his craft, [so] your thoughts should be corrupted from simplicity as to the Christ.
texts.2co.11.4: For if indeed he that comes preaches another Jesus, whom we have not preached, or ye get a different Spirit, which ye have not got, or a different glad tidings, which ye have not received, ye might well bear with [it].
texts.2co.11.5: For I reckon that in nothing I am behind those who are in surpassing degree apostles.
texts.2co.11.6: But if [I am] a simple person in speech, yet not in knowledge, but in everything making [the truth] manifest in all things to you.
texts.2co.11.7: Have I committed sin, abasing myself in order that *ye* might be exalted, because I gratuitously announced to you the glad tidings of God?
texts.2co.11.8: I spoiled other assemblies, receiving hire for ministry towards you.
texts.2co.11.9: And being present with you and lacking, I did not lazily burden any one, (for the brethren who came from Macedonia supplied what I lacked,) and in everything I kept myself from being a burden to you, and will keep myself.
texts.2co.11.10: [The] truth of Christ is in me that this boasting shall not be stopped as to me in the regions of Achaia.
texts.2co.11.11: Why? because I do not love you? God knows.
texts.2co.11.12: But what I do, I will also do, that I may cut off the opportunity of those wishing [for] an opportunity, that wherein they boast they may be found even as we.
texts.2co.11.13: For such [are] false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into apostles of Christ.
texts.2co.11.14: And [it is] not wonderful, for Satan himself transforms himself into an angel of light.
texts.2co.11.15: It is no great thing therefore if his ministers also transform themselves as ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.
texts.2co.11.16: Again I say, Let not any one think me to be a fool; but if otherwise, receive me then even as a fool, that *I* also may boast myself some little.
texts.2co.11.17: What I speak I do not speak according to [the] Lord, but as in folly, in this confidence of boasting.
texts.2co.11.18: Since many boast according to flesh, *I* also will boast.
texts.2co.11.19: For ye bear fools readily, being wise.
texts.2co.11.20: For ye bear if any one bring you into bondage, if any one devour [you], if any one get [your money], if any one exalt himself, if any one beat you on the face.
texts.2co.11.21: I speak as to dishonour, as though *we* had been weak; but wherein any one is daring, (I speak in folly,) *I* also am daring.
texts.2co.11.22: Are they Hebrews? *I* also. Are they Israelites? *I* also. Are they seed of Abraham? *I* also.
texts.2co.11.23: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as being beside myself) *I* above measure [so]; in labours exceedingly abundant, in stripes to excess, in prisons exceedingly abundant, in deaths oft.
texts.2co.11.24: From the Jews five times have I received forty [stripes], save one.
texts.2co.11.25: Thrice have I been scourged, once I have been stoned, three times I have suffered shipwreck, a night and day I passed in the deep:
texts.2co.11.26: in journeyings often, in perils of rivers, in perils of robbers, in perils from [my own] race, in perils from [the] nations, in perils in [the] city, in perils in [the] desert, in perils on [the] sea, in perils among false brethren;
texts.2co.11.27: in labour and toil, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
texts.2co.11.28: Besides those things that are without, the crowd [of cares] pressing on me daily, the burden of all the assemblies.
texts.2co.11.29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is stumbled, and I burn not?
texts.2co.11.30: If it is needful to boast, I will boast in the things which concern my infirmity.
texts.2co.11.31: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus knows -- he who is blessed for ever -- that I do not lie.
texts.2co.11.32: In Damascus the ethnarch of Aretas the king kept the city of the Damascenes shut up, wishing to take me;
texts.2co.11.33: and through a window in a basket I was let down by the wall, and escaped his hands.
texts.2co.12.1: Well, it is not of profit to me to boast, for I will come to visions and revelations of [the] Lord.
texts.2co.12.2: I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago, (whether in [the] body I know not, or out of the body I know not, God knows;) such [a one] caught up to [the] third heaven.
texts.2co.12.3: And I know such a man, (whether in [the] body or out of the body I know not, God knows;)
texts.2co.12.4: that he was caught up into paradise, and heard unspeakable things said which it is not allowed to man to utter.
texts.2co.12.5: Of such [a one] I will boast, but of myself I will not boast, unless in my weaknesses.
texts.2co.12.6: For if I shall desire to boast, I shall not be a fool; for I will say [the] truth; but I forbear, lest any one should think as to me above what he sees me [to be], or whatever he may hear of me.
texts.2co.12.7: And that I might not be exalted by the exceeding greatness of the revelations, there was given to me a thorn for the flesh, a messenger of Satan that he might buffet me, that I might not be exalted.
texts.2co.12.8: For this I thrice besought the Lord that it might depart from me.
texts.2co.12.9: And he said to me, My grace suffices thee; for [my] power is perfected in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather boast in my weaknesses, that the power of the Christ may dwell upon me.
texts.2co.12.10: Wherefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in insults, in necessities, in persecutions, in straits, for Christ: for when I am weak, then I am powerful.
texts.2co.12.11: I have become a fool; *ye* have compelled me; for *I* ought to have been commended by you; for I have been nothing behind those who were in surpassing degree apostles, if also I am nothing.
texts.2co.12.12: The signs indeed of the apostle were wrought among you in all endurance, signs, and wonders, and works of power.
texts.2co.12.13: For in what is it that ye have been inferior to the other assemblies, unless that I myself have not been in laziness a charge upon you? Forgive me this injury.
texts.2co.12.14: Behold, this third time I am ready to come to you, and I will not be in laziness a charge; for I do not seek yours, but you; for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.
texts.2co.12.15: Now *I* shall most gladly spend and be utterly spent for your souls, if even in abundantly loving you I should be less loved.
texts.2co.12.16: But be it so. *I* did not burden you, but being crafty I took you by guile.
texts.2co.12.17: Did I make gain of you by any of those whom I have sent to you?
texts.2co.12.18: I begged Titus, and sent the brother with [him]: did Titus at all make gain of you? have we not walked in the same spirit? [have we] not in the same steps?
texts.2co.12.19: Ye have long been supposing that we excuse ourselves to you: we speak before God in Christ; and all things, beloved, for your building up.
texts.2co.12.20: For I fear lest perhaps coming I find you not such as I wish, and that *I* be found by you such as ye do not wish: lest [there might be] strifes, jealousies, angers, contentions, evil speakings, whisperings, puffings up, disturbances;
texts.2co.12.21: lest my God should humble me as to you when I come again, and that I shall grieve over many of those who have sinned before, and have not repented as to the uncleanness and fornication and licentiousness which they have practised.
texts.2co.13.1: This third time I am coming to you. In the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every matter be established.
texts.2co.13.2: I have declared beforehand, and I say beforehand as present the second time, and now absent, to those that have sinned before, and to all the rest, that if I come again I will not spare.
texts.2co.13.3: Since ye seek a proof of Christ speaking in me, (who is not weak towards you, but is powerful among you,
texts.2co.13.4: for if indeed he has been crucified in weakness, yet he lives by God's power; for indeed *we* are weak in him, but we shall live with him by God's power towards you,)
texts.2co.13.5: examine your own selves if ye be in the faith; prove your own selves: do ye not recognise yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you, unless indeed ye be reprobates?
texts.2co.13.6: Now I hope that ye will know that *we* are not reprobates.
texts.2co.13.7: But we pray to God that ye may do nothing evil; not that *we* may appear approved, but that *ye* may do what is right, and *we* be as reprobates.
texts.2co.13.8: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.
texts.2co.13.9: For we rejoice when *we* may be weak and *ye* may be powerful. But this also we pray for, your perfecting.
texts.2co.13.10: On this account I write these things being absent, that being present I may not use severity according to the authority which the Lord has given me for building up, and not for overthrowing.
texts.2co.13.11: For the rest, brethren, rejoice; be perfected; be encouraged; be of one mind; be at peace; and the God of love and peace shall be with you.
texts.2co.13.12: Salute one another with a holy kiss.
texts.2co.13.14: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, [be] with you all.

texts.2co.1.1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, through the will of God, and Timotheus the brother, to the assembly of God that is in Corinth, with all the saints who are in all Achaia:
texts.2co.1.2: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ!
texts.2co.1.3: Blessed [is] God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of the mercies, and God of all comfort,
texts.2co.1.4: who is comforting us in all our tribulation, for our being able to comfort those in any tribulation through the comfort with which we are comforted ourselves by God;
texts.2co.1.5: because, as the sufferings of the Christ do abound to us, so through the Christ doth abound also our comfort;
texts.2co.1.6: and whether we be in tribulation, [it is] for your comfort and salvation, that is wrought in the enduring of the same sufferings that we also suffer; whether we are comforted, [it is] for your comfort and salvation;
texts.2co.1.7: and our hope [is] stedfast for you, knowing that even as ye are partakers of the sufferings -- so also of the comfort.
texts.2co.1.8: For we do not wish you to be ignorant, brethren, of our tribulation that happened to us in Asia, that we were exceedingly burdened above [our] power, so that we despaired even of life;
texts.2co.1.9: but we ourselves in ourselves the sentence of the death have had, that we may not be trusting on ourselves, but on God, who is raising the dead,
texts.2co.1.10: who out of so great a death did deliver us, and doth deliver, in whom we have hoped that even yet He will deliver;
texts.2co.1.11: ye working together also for us by your supplication, that the gift through many persons to us, through many may be thankfully acknowledged for us.
texts.2co.1.12: For our glorying is this: the testimony of our conscience, that in simplicity and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom, but in the grace of God, we did conduct ourselves in the world, and more abundantly toward you;
texts.2co.1.13: for no other things do we write to you, but what ye either do read or also acknowledge, and I hope that also unto the end ye shall acknowledge,
texts.2co.1.14: according as also ye did acknowledge us in part, that your glory we are, even as also ye [are] ours, in the day of the Lord Jesus;
texts.2co.1.15: and in this confidence I was purposing to come unto you before, that a second favour ye might have,
texts.2co.1.16: and through you to pass to Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come unto you, and by you to be sent forward to Judea.
texts.2co.1.17: This, therefore, counselling, did I then use the lightness; or the things that I counsel, according to the flesh do I counsel, that it may be with me Yes, yes, and No, no?
texts.2co.1.18: and God [is] faithful, that our word unto you became not Yes and No,
texts.2co.1.19: for the Son of God, Jesus Christ, among you through us having been preached -- through me and Silvanus and Timotheus -- did not become Yes and No, but in him it hath become Yes;
texts.2co.1.20: for as many as [are] promises of God, in him [are] the Yes, and in him the Amen, for glory to God through us;
texts.2co.1.21: and He who is confirming you with us into Christ, and did anoint us, [is] God,
texts.2co.1.22: who also sealed us, and gave the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.
texts.2co.1.23: And I for a witness on God do call upon my soul, that sparing you, I came not yet to Corinth;
texts.2co.1.24: not that we are lords over your faith, but we are workers together with your joy, for by the faith ye stand.
texts.2co.2.1: And I decided this to myself, not again to come in sorrow unto you,
texts.2co.2.2: for if I make you sorry, then who is he who is making me glad, except he who is made sorry by me?
texts.2co.2.3: and I wrote to you this same thing, that having come, I may not have sorrow from them of whom it behoved me to have joy, having confidence in you all, that my joy is of you all,
texts.2co.2.4: for out of much tribulation and pressure of heart I wrote to you through many tears, not that ye might be made sorry, but that ye might know the love that I have more abundantly toward you.
texts.2co.2.5: And if any one hath caused sorrow, he hath not caused sorrow to me, but in part, that I may not burden you all;
texts.2co.2.6: sufficient to such a one is this punishment, that [is] by the more part,
texts.2co.2.7: so that, on the contrary, [it is] rather for you to forgive and to comfort, lest by over abundant sorrow such a one may be swallowed up;
texts.2co.2.8: wherefore, I call upon you to confirm love to him,
texts.2co.2.9: for, for this also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether in regard to all things ye are obedient.
texts.2co.2.10: And to whom ye forgive anything -- I also; for I also, if I have forgiven anything, to whom I have forgiven [it], because of you -- in the person of Christ -- [I forgive it,]
texts.2co.2.11: that we may not be over-reached by the Adversary, for of his devices we are not ignorant.
texts.2co.2.12: And having come to Troas for the good news of the Christ, and a door to me having been opened in the Lord,
texts.2co.2.13: I have not had rest to my spirit, on my not finding Titus my brother, but having taken leave of them, I went forth to Macedonia;
texts.2co.2.14: and to God [are] thanks, who at all times is leading us in triumph in the Christ, and the fragrance of His knowledge He is manifesting through us in every place,
texts.2co.2.15: because of Christ a sweet fragrance we are to God, in those being saved, and in those being lost;
texts.2co.2.16: to the one, indeed, a fragrance of death to death, and to the other, a fragrance of life to life; and for these things who is sufficient?
texts.2co.2.17: for we are not as the many, adulterating the word of God, but as of sincerity -- but as of God; in the presence of God, in Christ we do speak.
texts.2co.3.1: Do we begin again to recommend ourselves, except we need, as some, letters of recommendation unto you, or from you?
texts.2co.3.2: our letter ye are, having been written in our hearts, known and read by all men,
texts.2co.3.3: manifested that ye are a letter of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God, not in the tablets of stone, but in fleshy tablets of the heart,
texts.2co.3.4: and such trust we have through the Christ toward God,
texts.2co.3.5: not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think anything, as of ourselves, but our sufficiency [is] of God,
texts.2co.3.6: who also made us sufficient [to be] ministrants of a new covenant, not of letter, but of spirit; for the letter doth kill, and the spirit doth make alive.
texts.2co.3.7: and if the ministration of the death, in letters, engraved in stones, came in glory, so that the sons of Israel were not able to look stedfastly to the face of Moses, because of the glory of his face -- which was being made useless,
texts.2co.3.8: how shall the ministration of the Spirit not be more in glory?
texts.2co.3.9: for if the ministration of the condemnation [is] glory, much more doth the ministration of the righteousness abound in glory;
texts.2co.3.10: for also even that which hath been glorious, hath not been glorious -- in this respect, because of the superior glory;
texts.2co.3.11: for if that which is being made useless [is] through glory, much more that which is remaining [is] in glory.
texts.2co.3.12: Having, then, such hope, we use much freedom of speech,
texts.2co.3.13: and [are] not as Moses, who was putting a vail upon his own face, for the sons of Israel not stedfastly to look to the end of that which is being made useless,
texts.2co.3.14: but their minds were hardened, for unto this day the same vail at the reading of the Old Covenant doth remain unwithdrawn -- which in Christ is being made useless --
texts.2co.3.15: but till to-day, when Moses is read, a vail upon their heart doth lie,
texts.2co.3.16: and whenever they may turn unto the Lord, the vail is taken away.
texts.2co.3.17: And the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord [is], there [is] liberty;
texts.2co.3.18: and we all, with unvailed face, the glory of the Lord beholding in a mirror, to the same image are being transformed, from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the Lord.
texts.2co.4.1: Because of this, having this ministration, according as we did receive kindness, we do not faint,
texts.2co.4.2: but did renounce for ourselves the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor deceitfully using the word of God, but by the manifestation of the truth recommending ourselves unto every conscience of men, before God;
texts.2co.4.3: and if also our good news is vailed, in those perishing it is vailed,
texts.2co.4.4: in whom the god of this age did blind the minds of the unbelieving, that there doth not shine forth to them the enlightening of the good news of the glory of the Christ, who is the image of God;
texts.2co.4.5: for not ourselves do we preach, but Christ Jesus -- Lord, and ourselves your servants because of Jesus;
texts.2co.4.6: because [it is] God who said, Out of darkness light [is] to shine, who did shine in our hearts, for the enlightening of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
texts.2co.4.7: And we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us;
texts.2co.4.8: on every side being in tribulation, but not straitened; perplexed, but not in despair;
texts.2co.4.9: persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;
texts.2co.4.10: at all times the dying of the Lord Jesus bearing about in the body, that the life also of Jesus in our body may be manifested,
texts.2co.4.11: for always are we who are living delivered up to death because of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our dying flesh,
texts.2co.4.12: so that, the death indeed in us doth work, and the life in you.
texts.2co.4.13: And having the same spirit of the faith, according to that which hath been written, `I believed, therefore I did speak;' we also do believe, therefore also do we speak;
texts.2co.4.14: knowing that He who did raise up the Lord Jesus, us also through Jesus shall raise up, and shall present with you,
texts.2co.4.15: for the all things [are] because of you, that the grace having been multiplied, because of the thanksgiving of the more, may abound to the glory of God;
texts.2co.4.16: wherefore, we faint not, but if also our outward man doth decay, yet the inward is renewed day by day;
texts.2co.4.17: for the momentary light matter of our tribulation, more and more exceedingly an age-during weight of glory doth work out for us --
texts.2co.4.18: we not looking to the things seen, but to the things not seen; for the things seen [are] temporary, but the things not seen [are] age-during.
texts.2co.5.1: For we have known that if our earthly house of the tabernacle may be thrown down, a building from God we have, an house not made with hands -- age-during -- in the heavens,
texts.2co.5.2: for also in this we groan, with our dwelling that is from heaven earnestly desiring to clothe ourselves,
texts.2co.5.3: if so be that, having clothed ourselves, we shall not be found naked,
texts.2co.5.4: for we also who are in the tabernacle do groan, being burdened, seeing we wish not to unclothe ourselves, but to clothe ourselves, that the mortal may be swallowed up of the life.
texts.2co.5.5: And He who did work us to this self-same thing [is] God, who also did give to us the earnest of the Spirit;
texts.2co.5.6: having courage, then, at all times, and knowing that being at home in the body, we are away from home from the Lord, --
texts.2co.5.7: for through faith we walk, not through sight --
texts.2co.5.8: we have courage, and are well pleased rather to be away from the home of the body, and to be at home with the Lord.
texts.2co.5.9: Wherefore also we are ambitious, whether at home or away from home, to be well pleasing to him,
texts.2co.5.10: for all of us it behoveth to be manifested before the tribunal of the Christ, that each one may receive the things [done] through the body, in reference to the things that he did, whether good or evil;
texts.2co.5.11: having known, therefore, the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, and to God we are manifested, and I hope also in your consciences to have been manifested;
texts.2co.5.12: for not again ourselves do we recommend to you, but we are giving occasion to you of glorifying in our behalf, that ye may have [something] in reference to those glorifying in face and not in heart;
texts.2co.5.13: for whether we were beside ourselves, [it was] to God; whether we be of sound mind -- [it is] to you,
texts.2co.5.14: for the love of the Christ doth constrain us, having judged thus: that if one for all died, then the whole died,
texts.2co.5.15: and for all he died, that those living, no more to themselves may live, but to him who died for them, and was raised again.
texts.2co.5.16: So that we henceforth have known no one according to the flesh, and even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know him no more;
texts.2co.5.17: so that if any one [is] in Christ -- [he is] a new creature; the old things did pass away, lo, become new have the all things.
texts.2co.5.18: And the all things [are] of God, who reconciled us to Himself through Jesus Christ, and did give to us the ministration of the reconciliation,
texts.2co.5.19: how that God was in Christ -- a world reconciling to Himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses; and having put in us the word of the reconciliation,
texts.2co.5.20: in behalf of Christ, then, we are ambassadors, as if God were calling through us, we beseech, in behalf of Christ, `Be ye reconciled to God;'
texts.2co.5.21: for him who did not know sin, in our behalf He did make sin, that we may become the righteousness of God in him.
texts.2co.6.1: And working together also we call upon [you] that ye receive not in vain the grace of God --
texts.2co.6.2: for He saith, `In an acceptable time I did hear thee, and in a day of salvation I did help thee, lo, now [is] a well-accepted time; lo, now, a day of salvation,' --
texts.2co.6.3: in nothing giving any cause of offence, that the ministration may be not blamed,
texts.2co.6.4: but in everything recommending ourselves as God's ministrants; in much patience, in tribulations, in necessities, in distresses,
texts.2co.6.5: in stripes, in imprisonments, in insurrections, in labours, in watchings, in fastings,
texts.2co.6.6: in pureness, in knowledge, in long-suffering, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love unfeigned,
texts.2co.6.7: in the word of truth, in the power of God, through the armour of the righteousness, on the right and on the left,
texts.2co.6.8: through glory and dishonour, through evil report and good report, as leading astray, and true;
texts.2co.6.9: as unknown, and recognized; as dying, and lo, we live; as chastened, and not put to death;
texts.2co.6.10: as sorrowful, and always rejoicing; as poor, and making many rich; as having nothing, and possessing all things.
texts.2co.6.11: Our mouth hath been open unto you, O Corinthians, our heart hath been enlarged!
texts.2co.6.12: ye are not straitened in us, and ye are straitened in your [own] bowels,
texts.2co.6.13: and [as] a recompense of the same kind, (as to children I say [it],) be ye enlarged -- also ye!
texts.2co.6.14: Become not yoked with others -- unbelievers, for what partaking [is there] to righteousness and lawlessness?
texts.2co.6.15: and what fellowship to light with darkness? and what concord to Christ with Belial? or what part to a believer with an unbeliever?
texts.2co.6.16: and what agreement to the sanctuary of God with idols? for ye are a sanctuary of the living God, according as God said -- `I will dwell in them, and will walk among [them], and I will be their God, and they shall be My people,
texts.2co.6.17: wherefore, come ye forth out of the midst of them, and be separated, saith the Lord, and an unclean thing do not touch, and I -- I will receive you,
texts.2co.6.18: and I will be to you for a Father, and ye -- ye shall be to Me for sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.'
texts.2co.7.1: Having, then, these promises, beloved, may we cleanse ourselves from every pollution of flesh and spirit, perfecting sanctification in the fear of God;
texts.2co.7.2: receive us; no one did we wrong; no one did we waste; no one did we defraud;
texts.2co.7.3: not to condemn you do I say [it], for I have said before that in our hearts ye are to die with and to live with;
texts.2co.7.4: great [is] my freedom of speech unto you, great my glory on your behalf; I have been filled with the comfort, I overabound with the joy on all our tribulation,
texts.2co.7.5: for also we, having come to Macedonia, no relaxation hath our flesh had, but on every side we are in tribulation, without [are] fightings, within -- fears;
texts.2co.7.6: but He who is comforting the cast-down -- God -- He did comfort us in the presence of Titus;
texts.2co.7.7: and not only in his presence, but also in the comfort with which he was comforted over you, declaring to us your longing desire, your lamentation, your zeal for me, so that the more I did rejoice,
texts.2co.7.8: because even if I made you sorry in the letter, I do not repent -- if even I did repent -- for I perceive that the letter, even if for an hour, did make you sorry.
texts.2co.7.9: I now do rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye were made sorry to reformation, for ye were made sorry toward God, that in nothing ye might receive damage from us;
texts.2co.7.10: for the sorrow toward God reformation to salvation not to be repented of doth work, and the sorrow of the world doth work death,
texts.2co.7.11: for, lo, this same thing -- your being made sorry toward God -- how much diligence it doth work in you! but defence, but displeasure, but fear, but longing desire, but zeal, but revenge; in every thing ye did approve yourselves to be pure in the matter.
texts.2co.7.12: If, then, I also wrote to you -- not for his cause who did wrong, nor for his cause who did suffer wrong, but for our diligence in your behalf being manifested unto you before God --
texts.2co.7.13: because of this we have been comforted in your comfort, and more abundantly the more did we rejoice in the joy of Titus, that his spirit hath been refreshed from you all;
texts.2co.7.14: because if anything to him in your behalf I have boasted, I was not put to shame; but as all things in truth we did speak to you, so also our boasting before Titus became truth,
texts.2co.7.15: and his tender affection is more abundantly toward you, remembering the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye did receive him;
texts.2co.7.16: I rejoice, therefore, that in everything I have courage in you.
texts.2co.8.1: And we make known to you, brethren, the grace of God, that hath been given in the assemblies of Macedonia,
texts.2co.8.2: because in much trial of tribulation the abundance of their joy, and their deep poverty, did abound to the riches of their liberality;
texts.2co.8.3: because, according to [their] power, I testify, and above [their] power, they were willing of themselves,
texts.2co.8.4: with much entreaty calling on us to receive the favour and the fellowship of the ministration to the saints,
texts.2co.8.5: and not according as we expected, but themselves they did give first to the Lord, and to us, through the will of God,
texts.2co.8.6: so that we exhorted Titus, that, according as he did begin before, so also he may finish to you also this favour,
texts.2co.8.7: but even as in every thing ye do abound, in faith, and word, and knowledge, and all diligence, and in your love to us, that also in this grace ye may abound;
texts.2co.8.8: not according to command do I speak, but because of the diligence of others, and of your love proving the genuineness,
texts.2co.8.9: for ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that because of you he became poor -- being rich, that ye by that poverty may become rich.
texts.2co.8.10: and an opinion in this do I give: for this to you [is] expedient, who not only to do, but also to will, did begin before -- a year ago,
texts.2co.8.11: and now also finish doing [it], that even as [there is] the readiness of the will, so also the finishing, out of that which ye have,
texts.2co.8.12: for if the willing mind is present, according to that which any one may have it is well-accepted, not according to that which he hath not;
texts.2co.8.13: for not that for others release, and ye pressured, [do I speak,]
texts.2co.8.14: but by equality, at the present time your abundance -- for their want, that also their abundance may be for your want, that there may be equality,
texts.2co.8.15: according as it hath been written, `He who [did gather] much, had nothing over; and he who [did gather] little, had no lack.'
texts.2co.8.16: And thanks to God, who is putting the same diligence for you in the heart of Titus,
texts.2co.8.17: because indeed the exhortation he accepted, and being more diligent, of his own accord he went forth unto you,
texts.2co.8.18: and we sent with him the brother, whose praise in the good news [is] through all the assemblies,
texts.2co.8.19: and not only so, but who was also appointed by vote by the assemblies, our fellow-traveller, with this favour that is ministered by us, unto the glory of the same Lord, and your willing mind;
texts.2co.8.20: avoiding this, lest any one may blame us in this abundance that is ministered by us,
texts.2co.8.21: providing right things, not only before the Lord, but also before men;
texts.2co.8.22: and we sent with them our brother, whom we proved in many things many times being diligent, and now much more diligent, by the great confidence that is toward you,
texts.2co.8.23: whether -- about Titus -- my partner and towards you fellow-worker, whether -- our brethren, apostles of assemblies -- glory of Christ;
texts.2co.8.24: the shewing therefore of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf, to them shew ye, even in the face of the assemblies.
texts.2co.9.1: For, indeed, concerning the ministration that [is] for the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you,
texts.2co.9.2: for I have known your readiness of mind, which in your behalf I boast of to Macedonians, that Achaia hath been prepared a year ago, and the zeal of you did stir up the more part,
texts.2co.9.3: and I sent the brethren, that our boasting on your behalf may not be made vain in this respect; that, according as I said, ye may be ready,
texts.2co.9.4: lest if Macedonians may come with me, and find you unprepared, we -- we may be put to shame (that we say not -- ye) in this same confidence of boasting.
texts.2co.9.5: Necessary, therefore, I thought [it] to exhort the brethren, that they may go before to you, and may make up before your formerly announced blessing, that this be ready, as a blessing, and not as covetousness.
texts.2co.9.6: And this: He who is sowing sparingly, sparingly also shall reap; and he who is sowing in blessings, in blessings also shall reap;
texts.2co.9.7: each one, according as he doth purpose in heart, not out of sorrow or out of necessity, for a cheerful giver doth God love,
texts.2co.9.8: and God [is] able all grace to cause to abound to you, that in every thing always all sufficiency having, ye may abound to every good work,
texts.2co.9.9: (according as it hath been written, `He dispersed abroad, he gave to the poor, his righteousness doth remain to the age,')
texts.2co.9.10: and may He who is supplying seed to the sower, and bread for food, supply and multiply your seed sown, and increase the fruits of your righteousness,
texts.2co.9.11: in every thing being enriched to all liberality, which doth work through us thanksgiving to God,
texts.2co.9.12: because the ministration of this service not only is supplying the wants of the saints, but is also abounding through many thanksgivings to God,
texts.2co.9.13: through the proof of this ministration glorifying God for the subjection of your confession to the good news of the Christ, and [for] the liberality of the fellowship to them and to all,
texts.2co.9.14: and by their supplication in your behalf, longing after you because of the exceeding grace of God upon you;
texts.2co.9.15: thanks also to God for His unspeakable gift!
texts.2co.10.1: And I, Paul, myself, do call upon you -- through the meekness and gentleness of the Christ -- who in presence, indeed [am] humble among you, and being absent, have courage toward you,
texts.2co.10.2: and I beseech [you], that, being present, I may not have courage, with the confidence with which I reckon to be bold against certain reckoning us as walking according to the flesh;
texts.2co.10.3: for walking in the flesh, not according to the flesh do we war,
texts.2co.10.4: for the weapons of our warfare [are] not fleshly, but powerful to God for bringing down of strongholds,
texts.2co.10.5: reasonings bringing down, and every high thing lifted up against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of the Christ,
texts.2co.10.6: and being in readiness to avenge every disobedience, whenever your obedience may be fulfilled.
texts.2co.10.7: The things in presence do ye see? if any one hath trusted in himself to be Christ's, this let him reckon again from himself, that according as he is Christ's, so also we [are] Christ's;
texts.2co.10.8: for even if also anything more abundantly I shall boast concerning our authority, that the Lord gave us for building up, and not for casting you down, I shall not be ashamed;
texts.2co.10.9: that I may not seem as if I would terrify you through the letters,
texts.2co.10.10: `because the letters indeed -- saith one -- [are] weighty and strong, and the bodily presence weak, and the speech despicable.'
texts.2co.10.11: This one -- let him reckon thus: that such as we are in word, through letters, being absent, such also, being present, [we are] in deed.
texts.2co.10.12: For we do not make bold to rank or to compare ourselves with certain of those commending themselves, but they, among themselves measuring themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are not wise,
texts.2co.10.13: and we in regard to the unmeasured things will not boast ourselves, but after the measure of the line that the God of measure did appoint to us -- to reach even unto you;
texts.2co.10.14: for not as not reaching to you do we stretch ourselves overmuch, for even unto you did we come in the good news of the Christ,
texts.2co.10.15: not boasting of the things not measured, in other men's labours, and having hope -- your faith increasing -- in you to be enlarged, according to our line -- into abundance,
texts.2co.10.16: in the [places] beyond you to proclaim good news, not in another's line in regard to the things made ready, to boast;
texts.2co.10.17: and he who is boasting -- in the Lord let him boast;
texts.2co.10.18: for not he who is commending himself is approved, but he whom the Lord doth commend.
texts.2co.11.1: O that ye were bearing with me a little of the folly, but ye also do bear with me:
texts.2co.11.2: for I am zealous for you with zeal of God, for I did betroth you to one husband, a pure virgin, to present to Christ,
texts.2co.11.3: and I fear, lest, as the serpent did beguile Eve in his subtilty, so your minds may be corrupted from the simplicity that [is] in the Christ;
texts.2co.11.4: for if, indeed, he who is coming doth preach another Jesus whom we did not preach, or another Spirit ye receive which ye did not receive, or other good news which ye did not accept -- well were ye bearing [it],
texts.2co.11.5: for I reckon that I have been nothing behind the very chiefest apostles,
texts.2co.11.6: and even if unlearned in word -- yet not in knowledge, but in every thing we were made manifest in all things to you.
texts.2co.11.7: The sin did I do -- myself humbling that ye might be exalted, because freely the good news of God I did proclaim to you?
texts.2co.11.8: other assemblies I did rob, having taken wages, for your ministration;
texts.2co.11.9: and being present with you, and having been in want, I was chargeable to no one, for my lack did the brethren supply -- having come from Macedonia -- and in everything burdenless to you I did keep myself, and will keep.
texts.2co.11.10: The truth of Christ is in me, because this boasting shall not be stopped in regard to me in the regions of Achaia;
texts.2co.11.11: wherefore? because I do not love you? God hath known!
texts.2co.11.12: and what I do, I also will do, that I may cut off the occasion of those wishing an occasion, that in that which they boast they may be found according as we also;
texts.2co.11.13: for those such [are] false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into apostles of Christ,
texts.2co.11.14: and no wonder -- for even the Adversary doth transform himself into a messenger of light;
texts.2co.11.15: no great thing, then, if also his ministrants do transform themselves as ministrants of righteousness -- whose end shall be according to their works.
texts.2co.11.16: Again I say, may no one think me to be a fool; and if otherwise, even as a fool receive me, that I also a little may boast.
texts.2co.11.17: That which I speak, I speak not according to the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this the confidence of boasting;
texts.2co.11.18: since many boast according to the flesh, I also will boast:
texts.2co.11.19: for gladly do ye bear with the fools -- being wise,
texts.2co.11.20: for ye bear, if any one is bringing you under bondage, if any one doth devour, if any one doth take away, if any one doth exalt himself, if any one on the face doth smite you;
texts.2co.11.21: in reference to dishonour I speak, how that we were weak, and in whatever any one is bold -- in foolishness I say [it] -- I also am bold.
texts.2co.11.22: Hebrews are they? I also! Israelites are they? I also! seed of Abraham are they? I also!
